source.original_text:
Under the common-sign independent block prior, the actual averaged Gaussian target factors into the product of the actual single-block mixtures and the residual standard Gaussian. \mathrm{split}_{\#} ar\pi_b=P_b^{\otimes k}\otimes\mathcal N(0,I_r). \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), with inclusive endpoints. Put \(k=\lfloor d/nfloor\) and \(r=d-kn=d mod n\). Fix one \(b\in\{-1,+1\}\). For full real orthogonal Haar probability \(\mu_n\), set \(
u_b=2\mu_n|_{\{\det O=b\}}\), and draw the blocks independently from this same fixed law. The signs are not drawn independently. The literal precision matrices are \(A_O= rac{\kappa+1}{2}I- rac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^	op)\) and \(A_{ oldsymbol O}=\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r)\). The actual matrix prior is \(\mathcal D_b=( oldsymbol O\mapsto A_{ oldsymbol O})_{\#}
u_b^{\otimes k}\). The actual laws are \(P_b=\int\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\,d
u_b(O)\) and \( ar\pi_b=\int\mathcal N(0,A^{-1})\,d\mathcal D_b(A)\). These are bind-mixtures of the canonical Gaussian constructor. They are not defined to be the claimed product. The matrix carrier uses its usual finite-dimensional Borel structure. The theorem proves that \(\mathcal D_b\), \(P_b\) and \( ar\pi_b\) are probabilities, and that \(A\succ0\) for \(\mathcal D_b\)-almost every \(A\). Positive definiteness, Gaussian-kernel measurability and mixture factorization are conclusions or internal producers, never caller hypotheses. The split takes consecutive coordinates \((x_j)_i=x_{jn+i}\) and \(z_t=x_{kn+t}\) in zero-based indices. It is the same coordinate bijection used by the literal block precision. No isometry for the ordinary product norm is asserted. If \(r=0\), the residual is the unique probability point mass on the zero-dimensional space; its unit factor agrees with the source omission convention.

∀ {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {b : ℝ} (hb : b = 1 ∨ b = -1),
    letI : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →
        (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) :=
      fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
        WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
    let ν := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))).restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = b}
    let D := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => ν)).map (fun O : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => Matrix.reindex e e (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => (((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • (((O j) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + ((O j) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)))) 0 0 (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)))
    let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    let P := ν.bind (fun O => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))⁻¹)
    IsProbabilityMeasure D ∧ (∀ᵐ A ∂D, A.PosDef) ∧
      IsProbabilityMeasure P ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure (D.bind γ) ∧
      (D.bind γ).map split = (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => P)).prod
        (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))))
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin m) is real m-dimensional Euclidean space with its usual Borel structure; Fin m indexes coordinates from zero. WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp preserve the entries. Ordinary finite function spaces and products carry product Borel structures and their usual default product norms.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) real is the full real orthogonal matrix group, with its usual topology and Borel structure, including either determinant sign. Matrix.PosDef means a real symmetric positive-definite matrix.

Measure.haarMeasure K is the canonical Haar measure normalized on the positive compact set K. TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts top is the entire compact group, so this constructor is its normalized Haar probability. Measure.restrict restricts a measure to a set; real nonnegative-infinite scalar multiplication has its usual meaning.

Matrix.reindex e e M has entries M (e.symm i) (e.symm j). Matrix.blockDiagonal f uses pairs (local coordinate, block index) and is zero between different blocks. Matrix.fromBlocks is the displayed two-by-two block assembly. finProdFinEquiv sends (a,b) to a times the cardinality of the second factor plus b; finSumFinEquiv concatenates its summands.

multivariateGaussian mean m covariance C is the pushforward of stdGaussian by z -> m + Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (CFC.sqrt C) z. The covariance interpretation holds when C is positive semidefinite; otherwise this total constructor defaults to a point mass. Matrix inverse is totalized at singular matrices.

stdGaussian is the standard Gaussian obtained by independent scalar standard normal coordinates in an orthonormal basis. On a zero-dimensional Euclidean space it is the probability point mass at its sole vector.

Measure.map is measurable pushforward; Measure.bind integrates the displayed measure-valued family. Measure.pi and Measure.prod are actual finite independent and binary products. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one, and the almost-everywhere quantifier is with respect to its displayed measure. Natural division and remainder and real scalar arithmetic have their ordinary Lean meanings.

quantifiers.original: For every admissible d,n,kappa and for each fixed b in {-1,+1}, draw the k O_j independently with the same mu_(n,b), then take the pushforward matrix law and average its Gaussian target. Equality is equality of probability measures, hence holds on every Borel event. There is no existential replacement family, no selected favorable prior, no almost-everywhere replacement of the law, and no universal mixed-sign pattern in Eq6.

A standard canonical identification or proved transport between block and flat coordinates is legitimate; arbitrary reinterpretation of the target is not. p_b and bar_p_b downstream denote actual densities of P_b and bar_pi_b.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianBlockLaw
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianMixtureLaws
import Mathlib.Probability.Independence.Integration
open Matrix MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped ENNReal
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.GaussianPrecisionDensity
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantFamily
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.DeterminantComponents
open AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianMixtureLaws

/-!
# Actual prior-averaged Gaussian block law

Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1, Section 3.1 Eq6. The matrix prior is the
actual pushforward of independent blocks with one common determinant sign.
The actual Gaussian bind is transported through the literal contiguous split.
Positive-definite support, normalization, measurable-family and averaging
producers are proved internally. Density/tensorization/amplification and the
main oracle lower bounds are distinct downstream obligations.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.AveragedBlockLaw
set_option autoImplicit false

theorem actual_averaged_block_product {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ) {b : ℝ} (hb : b = 1 ∨ b = -1) :
    letI : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →
        (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) :=
      fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
        WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
    let ν := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • (orthogonalHaar n).restrict
      {O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = b}
    let D := (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => ν)).map (blockPrecision κ)
    let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :=
      fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) A⁻¹
    let P := ν.bind (fun O => multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
      (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹)
    IsProbabilityMeasure D ∧ (∀ᵐ A ∂D, A.PosDef) ∧
      IsProbabilityMeasure P ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure (D.bind γ) ∧
      (D.bind γ).map split = (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => P)).prod
        (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))))
 := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let : MeasurableSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := borel _
  let : BorelSpace (Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) := ⟨rfl⟩
  let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
    ((Equiv.sumCongr
      ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
      (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
      (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
  let split : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) →
      (Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n)) :=
    fun x => (fun j => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j)))),
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))))
  let G := Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let En := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
  let Er := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (d % n))
  let ν := (2 : ℝ≥0∞) • (orthogonalHaar n).restrict
    {O : G | (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det = b}
  let f : (Fin (d / n) → G) → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ := blockPrecision κ
  let ρ := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => ν)
  let D := ρ.map f
  let γ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure E := fun A => multivariateGaussian (0 : E) A⁻¹
  let νr := stdGaussian Er
  let γn : G → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) := fun O =>
    multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (singleBlockPrecision κ O)⁻¹
  have hpriors := component_probabilities (lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn)
  have hν : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := by
    rcases hb with rfl | rfl
    · exact hpriors.2.2.1
    · exact hpriors.2.2.2
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure ν := hν
  have hf : Continuous f := by
    dsimp only [f]
    unfold blockPrecision singleBlockPrecision
    fun_prop
  have hfM : Measurable f := hf.measurable
  have hD : IsProbabilityMeasure D := Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hfM.aemeasurable
  have hpos (O : Fin (d / n) → G) : (f O).PosDef := by
    have hr := blockPrecision_regular hn hnd hκ O
    apply Matrix.posDef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec.mpr
    refine ⟨hr.1, fun v hv => ?_⟩
    have hdot : 0 < v ⬝ᵥ v := by
      simpa only [star_trivial] using (dotProduct_star_self_pos_iff.mpr hv)
    simpa only [star_trivial] using lt_of_lt_of_le hdot (hr.2 v).1
  have hcompact : IsCompact (Set.range f) := isCompact_range hf
  have hrange : ∀ᵐ A ∂D, A ∈ Set.range f := by
    rw [ae_iff]
    change (ρ.map f) (Set.range f)ᶜ = 0
    rw [Measure.map_apply hfM hcompact.isClosed.measurableSet.compl]
    simp
  have hDpos : ∀ᵐ A ∂D, A.PosDef := hrange.mono (by rintro A ⟨O, rfl⟩; exact hpos O)
  let q : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → E → ℝ := fun A x =>
    Real.sqrt A.det / (2 * Real.pi) ^ ((d : ℝ) / 2) *
      Real.exp (-((WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x)) / 2)
  let δ : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ → Measure E := fun A =>
    (volume : Measure E).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (q A x))
  have hq : Continuous (Function.uncurry q) := by dsimp only [q, E]; fun_prop
  have hδ : Measurable δ := measurable_withDensity (ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp hq.measurable)
  have hγ : AEMeasurable γ D := hδ.aemeasurable.congr (hDpos.mono fun A hA =>
    (multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity_of_posDef A hA).symm)
  have hP : IsProbabilityMeasure (ν.bind γn) := by
    have hl := actual_mixture_laws hn hκ
    rcases hb with rfl | rfl
    · exact hl.2.1
    · exact hl.2.2.1
  let P := ν.bind γn
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure P := hP
  let : IsProbabilityMeasure D := hD
  have hγn : Measurable γn := (actual_mixture_laws hn hκ).1
  have hγf : Measurable (fun O => γ (f O)) := by
    have heq : (fun O => γ (f O)) = δ ∘ f := by
      funext O
      exact multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity_of_posDef _ (hpos O)
    rw [heq]
    exact hδ.comp hfM
  let F := (Fin (d / n) → En) × Er
  let Tlin : E →ₗ[ℝ] F :=
    { toFun := split
      map_add' := by intro x y; ext i j <;> rfl
      map_smul' := by intro a x; ext i j <;> rfl }
  have hsplit : Measurable split := Tlin.toContinuousLinearMap.continuous.measurable
  have hc (O : Fin (d / n) → G) : (γ (f O)).map split =
      (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))).prod νr :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.GaussianBlockLaw.actual_conditional_block_product
      hn hnd hκ O
  have hfull : Measurable (fun O => (γ (f O)).map split) :=
    (Measure.measurable_map split hsplit).comp hγf
  have hπeq (O : Fin (d / n) → G) :
      ((γ (f O)).map split).map Prod.fst = Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j)) := by
    rw [hc, Measure.map_fst_prod]
    simp only [measure_univ, one_smul]
  have hπ : Measurable (fun O : Fin (d / n) → G => Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))) := by
    have heq : (fun O => ((γ (f O)).map split).map Prod.fst) =
        (fun O : Fin (d / n) → G => Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))) := funext hπeq
    rw [← heq]
    exact (Measure.measurable_map Prod.fst measurable_fst).comp hfull
  have hprod : Measurable (fun O : Fin (d / n) → G =>
      (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))).prod νr) := by
    have heq : (fun O => (γ (f O)).map split) =
        (fun O : Fin (d / n) → G => (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))).prod νr) := funext hc
    rw [← heq]
    exact hfull
  have hblocks : ρ.bind (fun O => Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))) =
      Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => P) := by
    symm
    apply Measure.pi_eq
    intro s hs
    rw [Measure.bind_apply (MeasurableSet.univ_pi hs) hπ.aemeasurable]
    simp_rw [Measure.pi_pi]
    let X : Fin (d / n) → G → ℝ≥0∞ := fun j O => γn O (s j)
    have hX (j : Fin (d / n)) : Measurable (X j) := (Measure.measurable_coe (hs j)).comp hγn
    have hI := iIndepFun_pi (μ := fun _ : Fin (d / n) => ν) (X := X)
      (fun j => (hX j).aemeasurable)
    have hfac := lintegral_prod_eq_prod_lintegral_of_indepFun Finset.univ
      (fun j (O : Fin (d / n) → G) => X j (O j)) hI
      (fun j => (hX j).comp (measurable_pi_apply j))
    change (∫⁻ O, ∏ j, X j (O j) ∂ρ) = ∏ j, P (s j)
    rw [hfac]
    apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
    intro j hj
    calc
      (∫⁻ O, X j (O j) ∂ρ) = ∫⁻ O, X j O ∂ν :=
        (measurePreserving_eval (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => ν) j).lintegral_comp (hX j)
      _ = P (s j) := (Measure.bind_apply (hs j) hγn.aemeasurable).symm
  have hjoint : ρ.bind (fun O => (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))).prod νr) =
      (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => P)).prod νr := by
    symm
    apply Measure.prod_eq
    intro s t hs ht
    rw [Measure.bind_apply (hs.prod ht) hprod.aemeasurable]
    simp_rw [Measure.prod_prod]
    have heval : Measurable (fun O : Fin (d / n) → G =>
        (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))) s) := (Measure.measurable_coe hs).comp hπ
    rw [lintegral_mul_const (μ := ρ) (f := fun O : Fin (d / n) → G =>
      (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))) s) (νr t) heval,
      ← Measure.bind_apply hs hπ.aemeasurable, hblocks]
  have hback : D.bind γ = ρ.bind (fun O => γ (f O)) := by
    change Measure.join ((ρ.map f).map γ) = Measure.join (ρ.map (fun O => γ (f O)))
    rw [hγ.map_map_of_aemeasurable hfM.aemeasurable]
    rfl
  have hpush : (D.bind γ).map split =
      ρ.bind (fun O => (Measure.pi (fun j => γn (O j))).prod νr) := by
    rw [hback]
    ext s hs
    rw [Measure.map_apply hsplit hs,
      Measure.bind_apply (hsplit hs) hγf.aemeasurable,
      Measure.bind_apply hs hprod.aemeasurable]
    apply lintegral_congr_ae
    exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun O => by
      have h := congrArg (fun μ => μ s) (hc O)
      rw [Measure.map_apply hsplit hs] at h
      exact h
  have htarget : IsProbabilityMeasure (D.bind γ) :=
    isProbabilityMeasure_bind hγ (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun A => by dsimp only [γ]; infer_instance)
  change IsProbabilityMeasure D ∧ (∀ᵐ A ∂D, A.PosDef) ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure P ∧
    IsProbabilityMeasure (D.bind γ) ∧ (D.bind γ).map split =
      (Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (d / n) => P)).prod νr
  exact ⟨hD, hDpos, hP, htarget, hpush.trans hjoint⟩

steps.title: Construct the true common-sign prior and its positive support
steps.text: The existing component-probability theorem normalizes the twice-restricted Haar laws. Their finite product is a probability, and the continuous literal block-precision map gives the actual matrix prior. The lower quadratic bound makes every image matrix positive definite. Its compact image has full prior mass, proving the almost-everywhere domain conclusion.
steps.formula: \nu_b(O(n))=1,\quad\mathcal D_b=f_{\#}\nu_b^{\otimes k},\quad I\preceq f(\boldsymbol O)\preceq\kappa I\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal D_b\{A:A\succ0\}=1.
steps.lean: hν calls component_probabilities; hf unfolds the unchanged precision formulas. hpos uses blockPrecision_regular; hcompact/hrange/hDpos prove the actual pushforward support, and hD proves probability.

steps.title: Produce measurability on the actual Gaussian domain
steps.text: Use the existing positive-definite precision-density theorem. The displayed density is jointly continuous as a real formula and defines a measurable withDensity family. On the actual positive-definite support it equals the canonical Gaussian. This proves almost-everywhere measurability under the matrix prior and pointwise family measurability along the block construction. The auxiliary density is not a new target definition, and no equality outside the positive-definite domain is used.
steps.lean: q, δ, hq and hδ use measurable_withDensity. hγ and hγf call the same canonical multivariateGaussian_eq_withDensity_of_posDef on hDpos/hpos. hγn and hP reuse actual_mixture_laws. The constructor fallback is outside these proved source domains.

steps.title: Reuse the fixed-tuple joint-law theorem
steps.text: Apply the one existing conditional block-product node at every tuple. The whole joint equality is retained. Its first projection also supplies measurability of the block-product kernel, so no product-kernel measurability assumption is added.
steps.lean: hc is an actual call to GaussianBlockLaw.actual_conditional_block_product. Tlin/hsplit give the exact measurable split; hfull, hπeq, hπ and hprod transport the actual kernels. This does not reproduce the conditional proof or create another canonical node.

steps.title: Average independent blocks and keep the residual factor
steps.text: On every measurable block rectangle, the product-kernel value is the product of its single-block values. The nonnegative integral product identity for independent coordinate variables and the evaluation pushforwards reduce this to the product of the true mixture values. Rectangle uniqueness identifies the block measures. The binary-product rectangle calculation then carries the common residual Gaussian through the same average. No finite real integral or independence estimate is supplied as a premise.
steps.lean: hblocks uses iIndepFun_pi, lintegral_prod_eq_prod_lintegral_of_indepFun, measurePreserving_eval, bind_apply and Measure.pi_eq. hjoint uses Measure.prod_eq and lintegral_mul_const. These are actual nonnegative finite-product integrations, including the zero-dimensional probability factor.

steps.title: Transport the actual matrix-prior average and consume it
steps.text: The pushforward-bind identity rewrites the actual average over matrices as the average of the prescribed full Gaussian over independent block tuples. Push the average through the measurable split and apply the conditional theorem and the preceding product calculation. The actual mixture is a probability. The focused consumer pushes this same full matrix-prior average to any block and to the residual, obtaining their genuine laws for every allowed parameter and either common sign.
steps.lean: hback is the real map-map/bind transport using hγ and hfM. hpush evaluates the real coordinate pushforward with hc, and htarget proves probability via isProbabilityMeasure_bind. reconstruction.text:
For every pair of natural numbers d and n, given 3 ≤ n and n ≤ d, for every real κ with 4 ≤ κ, and for every real b with b = 1 or b = −1, make the following definitions. The quantifier order in the displayed statement is d, n, the two dimension hypotheses, κ, its lower-bound hypothesis, b, and its sign hypothesis. There are no existentially quantified parameters.

Put q = d div n and r = d mod n. Thus d = qn + r, q ≥ 1, and 0 ≤ r < n. Write E_m = ℝ^m with coordinates indexed by Fin m = {0,…,m−1}, its Euclidean structure, and its usual Borel σ-algebra. The real d-by-d matrix space also carries its Borel σ-algebra. All finite function spaces and products below carry their usual product Borel structures.

Let O(n) be the full real orthogonal matrix group, containing both determinant signs, and let H_n be its Haar measure normalized to have mass one on the entire compact group. Define the finite measure ν on O(n) by
    ν(S) = 2 H_n(S ∩ {O ∈ O(n) : det O = b})
for measurable S. This is restriction to the determinant-b set followed by multiplication by the real nonnegative-infinite scalar 2; the definition is not an additional sampling hypothesis.

For O ∈ O(n), define the real n-by-n matrix
    B(O) = ((κ + 1)/2) I_n − ((κ − 1)/4)(O + Oᵀ).
For a family (O_j)_{j∈Fin q}, define A(O_0,…,O_{q−1}) as the d-by-d block matrix whose first q consecutive blocks are B(O_0),…,B(O_{q−1}), each of size n, and whose final block is I_r. All entries between distinct blocks are zero. More explicitly, A_{jn+i,kn+ℓ} is B(O_j)_{iℓ} if j = k and is zero if j ≠ k, for j,k ∈ Fin q and i,ℓ ∈ Fin n; A_{qn+s,qn+t} = δ_{st} for s,t ∈ Fin r; and entries between the first qn coordinates and the final r coordinates are zero. This ordering is exactly the reindexing obtained from the bijection e : ((Fin n × Fin q) ⊕ Fin r) → Fin d with e(inl(i,j)) = jn+i and e(inr(s)) = qn+s.

Let D be the pushforward of the finite product measure ν^{⊗q} under the map (O_j)_j ↦ A(O_0,…,O_{q−1}). Thus D is a measure on the Borel space of all real d-by-d matrices.

Use G_m(C) to denote the total multivariateGaussian constructor with mean 0 ∈ E_m and matrix argument C: it is the pushforward of the standard Gaussian on E_m under z ↦ (CFC.sqrt C)z. Its covariance interpretation is C when C is positive semidefinite, and the approved definition specifies a point mass otherwise. All matrix inverses used here are the totalized matrix inverse, including at singular matrices. Define the measure-valued function γ on every real d-by-d matrix by
    γ(A) = G_d(A⁻¹).
Define the measure P on E_n and the measure μ on E_d by the measure integrals
    P = ∫_{O∈O(n)} G_n(B(O)⁻¹) ν(dO),
    μ = ∫_A γ(A) D(dA) = D.bind γ.
These integrals are the displayed Measure.bind constructions.

Define the coordinate splitting map
    split : E_d → (Fin q → E_n) × E_r
by
    split(x) = (((x_{jn+i})_{i∈Fin n})_{j∈Fin q}, (x_{qn+s})_{s∈Fin r}).
The WithLp conversions in the displayed definition preserve all these coordinate entries. The target has the finite function-space and product Borel structures and their usual default product norms; the assertion below is an equality of measures on this target.

Then all of the following hold, as a conjunction:
(1) D is a probability measure.
(2) For D-almost every real d-by-d matrix A, A is real symmetric positive definite.
(3) P is a probability measure.
(4) μ = D.bind γ is a probability measure.
(5) The pushforward of μ under split satisfies the exact measure identity
    split_* μ = P^{⊗q} ⊗ stdGaussian(E_r).
Here P^{⊗q} is the actual finite independent product of q copies of P, and the rightmost product is the binary product with the standard Gaussian on E_r. Equivalently, under this pushforward law, the q displayed n-coordinate blocks have the independent common law P, and their joint law is independent of the final r-coordinate standard Gaussian. The positivity assertion has only the D-almost-everywhere scope stated in (2); on that set γ(A) has the usual centered Gaussian interpretation with covariance A⁻¹.

The lower endpoints n = 3 and κ = 4 are allowed, as is d = n. A zero remainder r = 0 is allowed: E_0 contains only its zero vector and stdGaussian(E_0) is the probability point mass at that vector. There is no upper bound on κ and no restriction on the remainder beyond natural division. The same b and κ are used for every block. No unspecified constant, asymptotic estimate, additional dimension hypothesis, metric identity, or pointwise-in-A positivity conclusion occurs in the proposition.
